sources.title: Anthropic: Claude-discovered ART enzyme system (Sep 23)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: Anthropic formed a life-sciences research group with a Bay Area wet lab (BSL-1/2, human scientists) and on Sep 23 reported Claude agents discovering ART, a previously uncharacterized phage enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeat arrays.
claims.context: First-party research announcement; lab existence and discovery report.

claims.text: Vendor-described method: ~950 agents, 21 hours, 210M tokens over DNA databases; 200k+ RTs to 3,500 candidates to 20 reports to 1 discovery; lab validation shows ART array expressed as short RNAs; function explicitly UNKNOWN; pre-print released, not peer-reviewed.
claims.context: Process facts vendor-stated; pre-review status and unknown function explicitly disclosed.

claims.text: Feng Zhang reviewed the pre-print and called the RNA-repeat/RT association genuinely intriguing and worth investigation.
claims.context: Cited third-party expert assessment, not independent replication.

limitations.text: Pre-print paper body not consumed; no verdict on evidence quality beyond announcement.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: "Autonomous discovery" is vendor framing: initial prompt and all lab work were human.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: No general scientific-capability inference beyond this single case; ART function unknown, no gene-editing utility established.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

targets.finding: Pre-print paper body not consumed; announcement-level facts verified but biological validity unreviewed; ART function unknown.
